title: What Happens If You Never Blink?
sources: American Academy of Ophthalmology, 'Why do we blink?' (average 15-20 blinks per minute; tears spread, cornea protected)
National Eye Institute, 'Blinking and eye health' (blinking keeps cornea moist; lack of blinking causes dry eye, corneal damage)
Cleveland Clinic, 'What happens if you don't blink?' (cornea can dry out in 10-15 seconds; damage begins within minutes)

lines.text: What happens if you never blink?
You blink about fifteen times a minute, mostly without noticing.
Every blink spreads a fresh layer of tears across your eye.
lines.caps: Every *blink | spreads | a fresh layer of *tears

lines.text: That keeps the surface smooth, clear, and protected from dust.
If you stop blinking, the tears evaporate in seconds.
The surface of your eye starts to dry out and crack.
lines.caps: Surface of your *eye | starts to *dry out | and *crack

lines.text: Within minutes, the cornea can become damaged and scarred.
Your vision blurs, then dims, and eventually you could lose sight.
lines.caps: Vision *blurs | then *dims | eventually | you could *lose sight

lines.text: So blinking is not a habit, it is a survival reflex.
lines.caps: Blinking is *not | a *habit | it is a *survival reflex

lines.text: Your eyes are basically tiny self-cleaning windows.
